title: NEB Class 12 Chemistry — Amines — 2024
subject: chemistry
source: NEB Grade 12 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Arrange the primary, secondary and tertiary amines in the order of basicity in aqueous solution and explain the order.
questions.solution:
In aqueous solution: **(C₂H₅)₂NH > (C₂H₅)₃N ≈ C₂H₅NH₂ > NH₃** for ethylamines.

The observed order is a balance of two opposing factors: the **+I effect** of alkyl groups increases electron density on nitrogen (raising basicity as the number of alkyl groups grows), while **solvation/stabilisation of the conjugate acid** (hydrogen bonding with water) decreases as N−H hydrogens are replaced, and steric hindrance around the lone pair reduces protonation for tertiary amines.
questions.knowledgeNote: In the gas phase basicity simply follows the +I effect: 3° > 2° > 1° > NH₃ — the reversal in water is the favourite NEB trap.

questions.question: Describe the Hinsberg test and use it to distinguish between primary, secondary and tertiary amines.
questions.solution:
Benzenesulphonyl chloride (C₆H₅SO₂Cl) reacts in aqueous alkali:

- **Primary amine:** forms a mono-substituted sulphonamide with an acidic N−H, so it dissolves in alkali to give a clear solution (soluble in KOH).
- **Secondary amine:** forms a di-substituted sulphonamide with no acidic hydrogen — insoluble in alkali, giving a precipitate.
- **Tertiary amine:** no reaction at all (no N−H to replace) and no precipitate; it remains as the free amine, distinguishable by odour and by its failure to react.
questions.knowledgeNote: Hinsberg's reagent separates the three classes in one test; the carbylamine (Hofmann isocyanide) test confirms a primary amine specifically.

questions.question: Write the reactions involved in the preparation and synthetic use of diazonium salts from aniline.
questions.knowledgeNote: Coupling of the diazonium ion with phenol or an aromatic amine gives the intensely coloured azo compounds — the key commercial use.
